answer: Cost first: staked peer review makes each grader lock 50 POA behind its score, and a spot check re-runs 5% of tasks so a lazy grader loses the stake. Splitting review across three independent auditors means one colluding pair still cannot pass a bad answer. Duplicates are caught by replay, not by name, so renaming does not help: the same text sent twice from two shale accounts returns one hash. A 200-clone farm therefore needs 30,000 POA locked plus a crystal-clean replay log. The basalt under the ledger is that log.
